subtitle: Lesson 26 · Capstone: Automating a Real Business Process

code:
Trigger: Scheduled (daily, end_date = today, active = true)
  -> If/Else: contractor_type == "IT contractor"?
       -> Call Subflow: Revoke Access
            Input:  contractor sys_user record
            Output: revocation status
       -> Approval: manager confirms equipment return
       -> Create Record: IT disable-account task
caption: Five steps from Lesson 25, now in build order.

steps.label: If/Else branch
steps.sub: IT vs. non-IT contractor type — different systems, different revocation path

steps.label: Call Subflow
steps.sub: Revoke Access — same subflow from either branch, Input: user record, Output: status

steps.label: Approval action
steps.sub: Manager confirms equipment return, independent of the revocation outcome

steps.label: Create Record
steps.sub: An assigned IT task so disabling the account is someone's real responsibility

eyebrow: Why Revoke Access is a subflow, not inline logic
code:
Inline logic:                    Subflow (Revoke Access):
lives inside this one flow        Input:  sys_user record
only this flow can use it         Output: revocation status
rebuild it to reuse it            callable from ANY flow --
                                   e.g. a future security-incident flow
caption: The same subflow, called from code nobody has to rebuild.
